detail.longDescription: In today’s # RCE …it’s # Ruby ’s turn. Wheee! On November 18, 2026, the Ruby core team disclosed seven vulnerabilities in Ruby’s regular expression engine and string case conversion, and released Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 to fix them. Ruby is an open-source programming language. It powers # RubyonRails and widely deployed products such as # GitLab , # GitHub Enterprise Server, # Mastodon and # Discourse . Because these flaws are in Ruby itself, every application on an affected Ruby version carries them, regardless of which gems it uses. All that said, execution of this flaw is a very high bar, so don’t set your hair on fire, but still patch. https://www. ox.security/blog/ruby2shell-ru by-memory-corruption-flaws-expose-applications-to-remote-code-execution-but-is-it-an-actual-risk/
